clues: A glacier can temporarily block a narrow channel and raise the water level behind it.
When that ice barrier fails, dramatic ruptures release water into the connected lake system.
Glaciers fed by a great Patagonian ice field calve into large, milky glacial lakes.
Rugged mountains and lakes form part of this protected landscape in southern Argentina.
Find the Argentine national park containing Perito Moreno Glacier and part of the enormous Lake Argentino.
targetLabel: Los Glaciares National Park — designated property reference point
modernContext: UNESCO’s published representative point for the designated property, not its uniquely correct centre.
explanation: The source describes the interaction of a glacier tongue, a narrow channel and changing lake levels. It does not establish a timetable for future rupture events. The park’s reference point represents a broad glacial landscape rather than the changing position of any individual ice front.
dateLabel: First UNESCO World Heritage inscription year, not the age of the natural feature
cultures: Physical geography, conservation and scientific study
uncertainty: Source-checked authoring only; independent factual, English and clue-order review is pending. The point represents the designated property, not every part of a large natural feature. Source descriptions and dynamic environmental conditions may differ in date or extent; precise current measurements are not implied.
